_comment: Constants for the energy model of EVALUATION.md section 4, in one place so
the GWDG reply and the section 8 sensitivity sweep are config edits rather
than code edits. Every value is tagged with its source; 'gwdg' means the
support reply of 2026-08-22 stated it, 'assumed' means we still do not know.
Consumed by: go run ./cmd/energy
What GWDG support confirmed, declined, and left unanswered. Recorded here
because the thesis constants table has to mark GWDG-provided values apart
from assumed ones, and because two of these are refusals rather than gaps:
asking again will not close them.
NOTE the reply is internally split: the generic 'is it 4x H100 PCIe on
KISSKI?' question was confirmed for the platform, but the precision answer
names our model specifically - 'FP8, wie zum Beispiel bei Devstral, das auf
2x H200 laeuft'. The model-specific statement governs: we cost Devstral,
not the platform average.

confirmed.platform: KISSKI inference platform is 4x H100 PCIe 80GB per node
confirmed.devstral_precision: FP8 (FP16 is the house default; Devstral is one of the FP8 exceptions)

declined.throughput_and_concurrency: data exists but may not be released - B stays the dominant unknown permanently, not pending

unanswered.pue: not answered; the 2021 Emmy press release remains the only source

hardware._source: gwdg (2x H200, per the 2026-08-22 reply) + NVIDIA H200 datasheet; node power still assumed
hardware._gpu_model: NVIDIA H200 SXM 141GB HBM3e (700 W). The reply did not name the variant; H200 NVL would be 600 W, which the node_power_watts sweep covers.
hardware._peak_flops_note: H200 FP8 tensor dense, 1979 TFLOP/s (3958 with sparsity, not used). FP8 is the right peak because the model is served in FP8; if the deployment were weight-only quantized (W8A8 vs W8A16) the math would run at the BF16 peak of 989 TFLOP/s - swept in sensitivity.peak_flops_per_gpu.
hardware._node_power_note: assumed: 2 x 700 W GPU + 2 x 150 W host/network share, keeping the same per-GPU host overhead the superseded 4x H100 figure used (600 W / 4 GPUs). GWDG did not supply a monitoring value.

_default._comment: Applied to any model in the run log without its own entry.
_default._source: devstral-2-123b-instruct-2512 model card; FP8 confirmed by GWDG 2026-08-22

_comment: Concurrency remains the single largest unknown; see section 8. GWDG holds
this data but declined to release it, so unlike the other gaps this one is
closed off rather than pending - the sweep over B is the permanent answer.
Two CO2 intensities, reported side by side (GHG Protocol Scope 2 dual
reporting). market_co2e_grams_per_kwh is GWDG's own basis - they stated
carbon-neutral operation - while grid_co2e_grams_per_kwh is what the
electricity physically drew from the German grid. Reporting only the
market figure would claim the energy was free; reporting only the location
figure would overstate what GWDG reports. Set market to null to drop the
second figure from the report.
facility._source: pue: GWDG press release 4/2021 (Emmy, 2021 - GWDG did not answer this, so it stays assumed); grid: Umweltbundesamt; market: gwdg (carbon-neutral, 2026-08-22)

_comment: The machine that runs the *pipeline*, not the inference node ([H5]).
It runs pyScan, go mod tidy, go build, one process per fixture per test
round, and Floci's emulator containers - and until 2026-09-04 it
contributed exactly zero to E_translation, which is why cmd/energy
printed 0.0 J against goBuilder and goTester.
The service now measures this directly: RAPL counters are read either
side of every job and recorded on the run log, so no constant is needed
and none is used when a measurement is present. These two values are the
fallback for run logs written before that (every run up to and including
20260831-190900) or produced on a host with no readable counter - WSL2,
macOS, most containers.
Both default to 0, which makes cmd/energy report host energy as NOT
COUNTED rather than invent it. That is the same rule cmd/runtime's
meters enforce: never report a joule that was not measured or explicitly
derived from a stated constant. Set fallback_power_watts to re-cost an
older run, and the figure is tagged ESTIMATED wherever it appears.
If you do set them: the run host is carl-eikermann-UX310UAK, an
ultraportable laptop. Measure it rather than guessing - the next metered
run reports its own idle baseline in the service log at startup.
host._source: measured per job when the host exposes RAPL; these fallbacks are assumed and must be tagged as such

_comment: repair_stages lists the pipeline task ids whose energy is repair rather
than first-pass translation, so the tool can report the repair share
without hardcoding task names it cannot know.
They must match the task ids of the pipeline that produced the run log
(default.json).
Ranges swept by -sweep to produce the section 8 table. The first three are
the parameters GWDG did not or would not supply; bytes_per_parameter is now
a counterfactual rather than an unknown (FP8 is confirmed) and is kept so
the table shows what the confirmation was worth.
